Hi Jane, Laura — quick technical note ahead of the diagrams.

1) Isolation model (summary):
- Dedicated mode: control plane is hosted by Redwood; compute (GPU pools) and network interfaces for Dedicated tenants are on isolated tenant pools. Tenant VPCs are customer-owned for Private, or dedicated VPC-like constructs for Redwood Dedicated with per-tenant NAT and security groups.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): customer-managed VPCs connect via private peering / VPN or direct connect. For on-prem deployments we ship an air-gapped bundle; network egress is disabled by default.

2) Shared vs dedicated components:
- Shared: control plane metadata services (management plane), billing/usage collectors (can be routed to customer-managed sinks on request).
- Dedicated: inference runtime, KV cache, GPU tenancy, and disk stores for model artifacts when requested.

3) Egress controls and firewall defaults:
- Default: outbound to vendor update endpoints and metrics collectors only. Customers may opt-in to block external egress; we can provide an allowlist for required endpoints.
- Inter-tenant traffic is blocked at the hypervisor/runtime; no tenant-to-tenant east-west permitted.

4) KMS/keys:
- Hosted: Redwood KMS with envelope encryption.
- Private: customer-managed KMS only (we provide HSM/KMS integration instructions and key rotation policies).

5) Logs & audit access:
- Audit logs are written to an internal write-once store and can be forwarded to customer SIEM via S3/GCS/Kafka. Retention: default 90 days; enterprise retention configurable.

I've attached the segment matrix (CSV) and a Visio diagram export for the private deployment. Laura/Aditya — I'll help review redacted exports before sharing publicly.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
